```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(car)
library(glmnet)
library(doParallel)
registerDoParallel(cores = detectCores() - 6)

data <- read_sav("data/data.sav")

subset <- data |> 
    select(Zage_screening, gender, Zdcog_ti, Zdsom_ti, nfc_group) |> 
    filter(nfc_group %in% c("2", "1")) |> # 2 is no need, 1 is unmet need 
    # but why only filter out these two groups??? oh for the logistic regression this is the response...
    # caption says 395 subset of people but dropping NAs removes a portion (9 people)
    drop_na() |> 
    mutate(nfc_group = as_factor(nfc_group),
           nfc_group = relevel(nfc_group, ref = "No need"),
           gender = as_factor(gender))

# data |> 
#     select(nfc_group)

paper_model <- glm(nfc_group ~ Zage_screening + gender + Zdcog_ti * Zdsom_ti, family = "binomial", data = subset)

summary(paper_model)

Anova(paper_model, test.statistic = "Wald") # this is what the paper has

# Prefer this
# Anova(paper_model, test.statistic = "LR")
```

## Paper Investigation

```{r}
test <- data |> 
    select(bdi1r:bdi21r, dcog_ti, dsom_ti, Zdsom_ti, Zdcog_ti, nfc_group, Zage_screening, gender) |> 
    filter(nfc_group %in% c("2", "1")) |> 
    rowwise() |> 
    mutate(sum_dcog = sum(c_across(bdi1r:bdi14r), na.rm = T),
           sum_dsom = sum(c_across(bdi15r:bdi21r), na.rm = T)) |> 
    ungroup() |> 
    mutate(zsum_dcog = scale(sum_dcog),
           zsum_dsom = scale(sum_dsom)) |> 
    mutate(nfc_group = as_factor(nfc_group),
           nfc_group = relevel(nfc_group, ref = "No need"),
           gender = as_factor(gender))

    # filter(!(Zdsom_ti == zsum_dsom))

paper_model <- glm(nfc_group ~ Zage_screening + gender + zsum_dcog * zsum_dsom, family = "binomial", data = test)

summary(paper_model)

Anova(paper_model, test.statistic = "Wald") # this is what the paper has
```

```{r}
set.seed(204)
cleaned_data <- data |> 
    filter(nfc_group %in% c(1, 2)) |> 
    mutate(nfc_group = factor(nfc_group)) |> 
    select(nfc_group, bdi1r:bdi21r, Zage_screening, gender) |> 
    drop_na()

X <- cleaned_data |> 
    select(!nfc_group)
y <- cleaned_data |> 
    select(nfc_group) |> 
    mutate(nfc_group = ifelse(nfc_group == 1, 1, 0))

cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(as.matrix(X), as.matrix(y), family = "binomial", nfolds = 20,
                      nlambda = 200, standardize = F, parallel = T, alpha = 1,
                      type.measure = "auc")


best <- glmnet(as.matrix(X), as.matrix(y), family = "binomial", alpha = 1, 
             lambda = cv_lasso$lambda.1se, type.measure = "auc", standardize = F)
coef(best)

plot(cv_lasso)

plot(best)
```

## Compare all questions vs. the 3 variables chosen
```{r}
all_data <- data |> 
    drop_na(Zage_screening, gender, bdi1r:bdi21r, nfc_group) |> 
    select(Zage_screening, gender, bdi1r:bdi21r, nfc_group) |> 
    filter(nfc_group %in% c("2", "1")) |> # 2 is no need, 1 is unmet need 
    # but why only filter out these two groups??? oh for the logistic regression this is the response...
    # caption says 395 subset of people but dropping NAs removes a portion (9 people)
    # drop_na() |> 
    mutate(nfc_group = as_factor(nfc_group),
           nfc_group = relevel(nfc_group, ref = "No need"),
           gender = as_factor(gender))

mini_data <- data |> 
    drop_na(Zage_screening, gender, bdi1r:bdi21r, nfc_group) |> 
    select(Zage_screening, gender, bdi5r, bdi17r, nfc_group) |> 
    filter(nfc_group %in% c("2", "1")) |> # 2 is no need, 1 is unmet need 
    # but why only filter out these two groups??? oh for the logistic regression this is the response...
    # caption says 395 subset of people but dropping NAs removes a portion (9 people)
    # drop_na() |> 
    mutate(nfc_group = as_factor(nfc_group),
           nfc_group = relevel(nfc_group, ref = "No need"),
           gender = as_factor(gender))

all_test <- glm(nfc_group ~ ., data = all_data,
                  family = "binomial")

quick_test <- glm(nfc_group ~ bdi5r + bdi17r + Zage_screening, data = mini_data,
                  family = "binomial")


anova(quick_test, all_test)
```

P-value = 0.2 about so little evidence the more complex model is significantly better
